newsitem.title: CANADA: Amer Sensors to seek bankruptcy protection.
newsitem.headline: Amer Sensors to seek bankruptcy protection.

text.p: American Sensors Inc said on Tuesday it will seek bankruptcy protection later this afternoon after Toronto-Dominion Bank and Comerica Bank called in loans totalling US$9.2 million dollars.

American Sensors said it received approval for a consolidated line of credit for US$22.5 million from the Credit Committee of Congress Financial Corp (Canada) for its North American and international operations.

The company, which develops early warning detection devices for home air quality safety, said it will seek protection under the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (CCAA) to permit refinancing and restructuring of its organization.

American Sensors said TD, which had delivered on March 12 a ten-day demand for repayment of its outstanding loans, informed American Sensors that it intends to enforce its security on March 26. The total amount owing to TD is US$8.1 million which includes a term loan of US$1.7 million.
Comerica Bank has also demanded repayment of a term loan in the amount of US$1.1 million, American Sensors said.

It said the new US$22.5 million credit line represents an increase of US$2.5 million over the line of credit currently in place with TD. The asset-based arrangement is projected to provide on the scheduled closing of March 31 about US$12 million in cash, which will be used to retire the TD operating bank loan of US$6.4 million.
American Sensors said it is examining all available options regarding the retirement of its term loans.
